B3.title: real-pair pool scaling at fixed compute (is Phase A pair-starved?)
B3.question: H1 (UNCHANGED): is Phase A pair-starved -- would more unique training pairs improve out-of-domain retrieval?
B3.lever: nested random subsets of the Phase-A pair pool at fractions {0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00}. NESTED (0.25 subset of 0.50 subset of 0.75 subset of full) so no between-arm sampling noise enters the contrast.
B3.held_fixed: 2,500 updates, batch 512, n_neg 32,768, LR, temperature, negative construction, AND the same Phase-B checkpoint p35b-2m. Total draws are therefore identical at 1,280,000 in every arm: compute is fixed and ONLY the unique-pair count varies, i.e. the treatment is diversity-versus-repetition at fixed budget.
B3.endpoint: TWO scalars, both pinned exactly, both read at int8 / sqrt (the release format and R0's adopted pooling rule). DENSE = the out-of-domain macro (equal-weight mean of nDCG@10 over cqadup-programmers and cqadup-physics). FUSED = the 4-component `fused_macro` over nq-250k, hotpotqa, cqadup-programmers and cqadup-physics under the FROZEN fusion operator. The group-vector median over three dev groups is reported DESCRIPTIVELY and binds nothing.
B3.bar: Evaluated in this order, on the two pinned scalars above. (1) MANIPULATION CHECK: the 1.00-vs-0.25 gain must reach >= 0.0040 on BOTH scalars. If it does not, the lever moved nothing this instrument resolves and the probe reports UNINFORMATIVE. (2) PRIMARY CONTRAST: 1.00 vs 0.50 -- mean-over-seeds gain >= 0.0040 on BOTH scalars -> PASS, 'Phase A is pair-starved at the frozen recipe'. (3) If the primary fails but the manipulation check passed -> FAIL, worded ONLY as stated in `fail_wording`. (4) NEGATIVE-DOSE, checked before (1) and defined as the mirror of the bar so it needs no separate machinery: if the 1.00-vs-0.25 mean gain is <= -0.0040 on BOTH scalars, more distinct pairs made the table WORSE at fixed compute. That is a finding about pool quality in its own right and is reported as such, never folded into FAIL or UNINFORMATIVE.
B3.multiplicity: none. The manipulation check is a hierarchical gate, the two scalars are an intersection-union (requiring BOTH is conservative, not double jeopardy), and the bar sits about 4 sigma above the measured dense floor and about 6 above the fused one. The conjunction only lowers type-I.
B3.seeds: THREE per fraction, paired: every arm inits from the same Phase-B checkpoint p35b-2m and differs only in the Phase-A seed. Fraction 1.00 is already on disk as `m8nf-seed0`, `m8nf-seed1`, `m8nf-seed2` -- verified config-identical to the f=1.00 arm (n_train_pairs 338,076; only the seed differs) -- so they ARE the 1.00 arms and are not retrained. Three rather than two because sign agreement at n=2 is nearly vacuous (P = 0.25 under the null against a bar at roughly 4 sigma) while costing real power near the bar.
B3.no_survivor: Phase-A-side pair-count levers at the FROZEN Phase-B checkpoint are deprioritised. Deliberately narrower than the first version, which deprioritised ICT, doc2query and more-real-pairs outright: `p35b-2m` ran 16,000 objective-B steps over the full pair query set, so EVERY arm -- 0.25 included -- inherits a table that has already seen all ~338K training queries and their teacher vectors. This probe therefore measures the marginal value of distinct pairs IN PHASE A GIVEN B absorbed them. A B-side pair lever flows through a leg this design holds fixed and needs its own evidence.
B3.prior: M7's clean-stack-tax arm added 490,241 real pairs for +0.0058 [-0.0015, +0.0131], unresolved -- but it held A-steps fixed, so exposure per pair fell as pairs were added and the two effects were confounded. This design separates them by holding total draws fixed and varying only the unique-pair count.

bar_frozen.read_at: int8 / sqrt -- the release format and R0's adopted pooling rule

B3.implementation_constraint: G3 forbids editing m7src, and no pair-fraction knob exists in m7src/train.py's Cfg. The fraction must therefore be applied by an m8src-side wrapper over train.kept_pairs -- which means the treatment does NOT appear in the run's cfg or meta.json. The fraction MUST therefore be encoded in the run id AND written to a stamped sidecar; see CODEMAP 16 for why an unrecorded treatment is the dangerous case.
B3.supersedes: the ICT-fraction registration of 2026-08-29, retired the same day before any arm ran (see B3-ICT and LEDGER 15).

pool_size.note: THREE different counts exist in this project and they are not interchangeable. `train.kept_pairs()` returns 340,850 decontaminated TRAIN pairs -- that is the list the fraction is applied to. `build_arrays` then drops pairs whose positives are banned or unresolvable, leaving the 338,076 the run records as `n_train_pairs`. Neither is the 337,981 of `results/m8_fitlist.json`, which is the CLOSED-FORM TABLE's fit list and has nothing to do with Phase A. The first version of this registration cited 337,981; corrected 2026-08-29 before any arm ran.
pool_size.source_share_note: uniform subsetting preserves these shares in expectation and, being a fixed-permutation prefix, up to hypergeometric noise. mrtydi-en is the thin one at 0.97% (3,310 pairs), so the 0.25 arm holds roughly 828 of them -- small, but not a regime where the source disappears.

B3.endpoint_correction: The ICT registration said the endpoint included the group-vector median over all three dev groups and that it was 'UNCHANGED, which is why the measured floors still bind'. That was FALSE for the fused half: the two held-out dev components carry pool row indices rather than document text, so no fused read exists for them by construction, and the fused floor of 0.00066 was measured on the 4-component fused_macro -- a different scalar from the one the endpoint text named. The endpoint is now pinned to the quantities the floors actually measured. Corrected 2026-08-29 before any arm was scored.
B3.primary_contrast_rationale: The primary was 1.00 vs 0.75 and is now 1.00 vs 0.50. At fixed total draws the fractions are epochs -- 1.00 is 3.8 epochs, 0.75 is 5.1 -- and a learning curve roughly linear in log(pairs) puts only about log(4/3)/log(4) = 21% of the 0.25->1.00 gain in the last quarter. So the 0.75->1.00 segment is the least-powered part of the curve: the design could clear the manipulation check at twice the bar while the primary segment's TRUE effect sat under it, and then declare 'not starved' while the curve was still climbing. 1.00 vs 0.50 is a single pre-specified contrast that carries about half the curve, and 'what does doubling the pool buy' is the actual M8 budget question. The log-slope of endpoint against log(pairs) over all four fractions is reported alongside, DESCRIPTIVELY.
B3.decision_statistic: mean over the three seeds of the per-seed gain, on each pinned scalar. Seed sign agreement is REPORTED but is not a gate -- it was a gate in the first version and is dropped: at n=2 it added almost no evidence and removed about 30% of the power near the bar.
B3.fail_wording: No rise of at least 0.0040 from half the pool to all of it, at the frozen 2,500-step Phase-A recipe on top of a Phase-B checkpoint that had already distilled on every training query.
B3.uninformative_action: UNINFORMATIVE is not a null result and not a pass. Given the floors already show the instrument resolves 0.0040, a 4x dose that moves neither scalar that far is itself the strongest no-starvation evidence this probe can produce -- it is recorded as such, and the pair-count levers are deprioritised on the same narrowed scope as `no_survivor`.
known_biases: The frozen fusion operator (convex0, w=0.8) was SELECTED on p35w-2m-s2500, i.e. on the f=1.00 recipe. Arms with a weaker dense side are read under a weight optimal for the comparator, which biases the FUSED scalar TOWARD passing. The dense scalar carries no such bias and both must pass.

One permutation. The 'last half' is a single fixed draw, so the contrast estimates the effect of THOSE pairs; the three seeds cover training noise only. A second pool seed must NOT be added after seeing a near-bar number.
B3.implemented_by: m8src/b3_decide.py -- the bar runs as code and writes its own verdict; the registry is read, not restated.
fail_wording_prohibits: any statement about pair-count levers in general
any statement about B-side pair levers, which this design holds fixed

NF.title: noise-floor measurement (the instrument every bar is set against)
NF.question: How large is a difference this dev instrument produces from nothing at all?
NF.endpoint: group_vector_median, worst_group, out_of_domain_macro and all_component_macro on the full pinned dev suite, int8, through the released QueryTable path
NF.comparator: K=3 arms of the IDENTICAL recipe, identical data, identical B checkpoint, differing ONLY in training seed (a true null)
NF.bar: no bar: this measures the instrument and adopts nothing. It EMITS bars: floor(endpoint) = max of the 3 pairwise |delta|; bar(endpoint) = max(0.0040, 2 x floor(endpoint)).
NF.no_survivor: not applicable -- a floor always exists. If the floor exceeds the planning minimum on an endpoint, every bar reading that endpoint rises accordingly and that is the finding.
NF.also_published: the +/-10% A-steps arms, as RECIPE SENSITIVITY beside the floor, never as the floor: a step change is a treatment, not a null
NF.frame_disclosure: measured in the incumbent teacher frame and the M7 data mix, A leg only with the B checkpoint fixed. An arm differing in its B leg has a larger floor and no bar may read such an arm until that floor is measured too.

B3-ICT.title: ICT (Inverse Cloze Task) pair augmentation
B3-ICT.question: does adding synthetic ICT pairs to Phase A improve out-of-domain retrieval?
B3-ICT.status: REGISTERED BUT REFUSED. This was B3's original lever; an adversarial review of the arm definition (2026-08-29, before any arm ran) found it could not answer B3's question and carried a pathology that would make a null result uninformative.
blockers: SHORTCUT IN THE TARGET. An ICT pseudo-query is a literal substring of its positive. Removing the sampled sentence from the positive does NOT remove the shortcut unless the frozen teacher vector is RECOMPUTED from the ablated context -- the precomputed pool vector still encodes the sentence. So the cheap version of the fix does not work.
COST. The repair therefore requires re-encoding one ablated context per ICT pair with the teacher, which the cheap design avoided entirely.
TRAIN/DEPLOY MISMATCH. Ablated-context vectors are not what is served; deployed document vectors are full documents. The cosine shift between the two would have to be measured and reported.

ESTIMAND. Adding synthetic pairs at fixed compute measures whether spending Phase-A budget on ICT helps -- not whether Phase A is pair-starved. B3's question is answered by the pool-scaling design instead.
B3-ICT.if_reopened: use the sampled sentence as query, form the positive from surrounding context with that sentence removed (ORQA removes it in 90% of examples, retaining 10% deliberately), RE-ENCODE that ablated context, filter empty/short contexts and near-duplicate sentences, and enforce at most one example per document per batch so sibling spans cannot act as each other's negatives.
B3-ICT.bar: TBD -- and deliberately so. This row is a REFUSAL kept for the record, not a probe awaiting a number: the blockers below are design faults, not a missing floor, so a bar must not be written for it until they are answered.
B3-ICT.bar_pending: the four blockers below; a bar written before them would be a bar for a probe that cannot answer its question
B3-ICT.endpoint: would inherit B3's, but see blockers -- the estimand itself is wrong for B3's question

E14-HEAD.title: doc-side re-shaping: RENORMALIZED heads on cached document vectors, trained with the table
E14-HEAD.question: Dylan's E14 ruling was 'measure it small first'. This is the small measurement: can the document space be re-shaped to be more reachable by a bag of token vectors AT ALL, before anyone pays to fine-tune the tower?
E14-HEAD.amended: 2026-08-29, after a Codex adversarial review of the design found three BLOCKERs, before any arm ran. The previous row's central premise -- 'a linear doc-side map is provably absorbable, so the head must be nonlinear' -- was FALSE and contradicted this ledger's own section 6 D1 entry. See LEDGER 15.
E14-HEAD.lever: TWO doc-side heads over the FROZEN teacher's cached document vectors, both of the form normalize(d + f(d)) with f zero-initialised: LIN, f(d) = W d (1024x1024, ~1.05M params) -- the PRIMARY; and MLP, f(d) = W2 GELU(W1 d + b1) (hidden 2048, ~4.2M params) -- the SECONDARY, which is also LIN's control: it is what says whether nonlinearity bought anything the linear map did not.
E14-HEAD.why_a_linear_head_is_NOT_a_no-op: the retired row asserted it was. It is not: retrieval L2-normalizes documents, so the score is q.(Md)/|Md| and the per-document factor 1/|Md| cannot move into a shared query row. results/m7_absorb_check.json measures rank agreement with the absorbed form at 1.000 WITHOUT renormalization and 0.000 WITH it, and LEDGER section 6's D1 entry already recorded this as 'the absorbable dismissal was half wrong'. A renormalized linear head is genuine document-side capacity, and it is the cheaper and better-conditioned probe.
E14-HEAD.why_it_is_cheap: the transformer is never re-run. The head is applied to document vectors already on disk, so re-encoding is a matmul over cached fp16 rather than 2M+ forward passes.
E14-HEAD.held_fixed: the query side stays a pure lookup table (E1), the teacher weights are untouched, Phase A/B structure, updates, batch, negatives, temperature, table learning rate and the pair pool are all as R0. The reported arms train on the FULL pair pool, not the ladder's holdout-reduced pool.
E14-HEAD.endpoint: the SAME two scalars as B3, both at int8/sqrt: DENSE = out-of-domain macro over cqadup-programmers and cqadup-physics; FUSED = the 4-component fused_macro under the frozen operator.
E14-HEAD.comparator: R0N -- the SAME patched path with the head FROZEN AT IDENTITY, three paired seeds. NOT the existing R0 arms. At W=0 the head emits normalize(d) while R0 scores the raw cached fp16 vectors, and those are only approximately unit-norm: over 100,000 sampled pool rows only 0.36% have float32 norm exactly 1, max |norm-1| = 4.8e-05, mean 9.1e-06. Renormalization shifts Phase-A logits and therefore the training trajectory, so R0 is not the exact comparator to a head-bearing arm. R0N against the existing R0 is ALSO reported, as an end-to-end null on the whole patch stack.
E14-HEAD.bar: mean-over-seeds gain >= 0.0040 on BOTH scalars, per head. 0.0040 is max(planning minimum, 2 x measured floor) at int8/sqrt; the endpoints and their floors are unchanged by this amendment, so the bar is unchanged.
E14-HEAD.seeds: 3 (0, 1, 2), paired: same Phase-B checkpoint, differing only in the Phase-A seed. The learning-rate ladder runs on a DISJOINT tuning seed (3) and its arms are never part of the reported mean.
E14-HEAD.multiplicity: TWO treatments (LIN, MLP), each read on two scalars. Intersection-union WITHIN a treatment (both scalars must clear, which only lowers type-I). Holm ACROSS the two treatments, because the probe's question -- does ANY cheap doc-side head clear -- is a union and the multiplicity is real.
E14-HEAD.head_lr_selection: ladder {3e-4, 1e-3, 3e-3} on tuning seed 3, selected on InfoNCE over a held-out 2% slice of the TRAINING pairs. The ladder subprocess is DEV-BLIND BY CONSTRUCTION, not by promise: train.run() evaluates cfg.eval_components every eval_every steps AND once more unconditionally at the end, and those components include both DENSE endpoint components, so a ladder that merely promised to ignore dev would still have observed it. dev_eval.eval_table is patched to raise in the ladder process. NOTE the holdout is held out from E14's Phase A only -- p35b-2m already distilled on every one of those queries and used their positives in its KL candidate sets.
E14-HEAD.step_adequacy: PRE-REGISTERED, and it gates the null. On tuning seed 3, continue the winning arm from 2500 to 5000 steps reading ONLY the training-holdout statistic. Plateau rule: the holdout improvement over 2500->5000 must be under 25% of the improvement over 1250->2500. If it is not, the primary reports OPTIMIZATION-INADEQUATE / UNINFORMATIVE and NOT a method null -- a null at an inadequate step budget is evidence about the configuration, not the method (CLAUDE.md standing directive #2).
E14-HEAD.mechanism_control: DESCRIPTIVE, does not gate the bar, and is what makes a positive interpretable. Score the headed documents against the FROZEN TEACHER query vectors as well as against the bag, giving {raw, headed} x {teacher queries, bag}. The head is supervised document-side metric learning and can win by fixing the teacher's relevance geometry or by separating training sources -- HotpotQA is ~85% of the document pool but ~24% of positive pairs -- none of which requires documents to have been bag-unreachable. The BAG gain MINUS the TEACHER-QUERY gain is the bag-specific evidence.
E14-HEAD.no_survivor: THE CHEAP RE-SHAPING DOES NOT HELP. This does NOT close E14 and must never be written as though it did -- see scope_limit. It means the head route is dead and the LoRA question stands, with its cost known.
E14-HEAD.scope_limit: THREE limits, all binding. (1) AN MLP OR LINEAR MAP ON THE FINAL DOCUMENT VECTOR CANNOT RECOVER INFORMATION THE TOWER DISCARDED, so this tests 'is the document space re-shapeable', NOT 'can the tower learn to be bag-reachable' -- E14's actual question. A null is therefore WEAK evidence about the LoRA and a positive is STRONG evidence FOR it; the asymmetry is the point of running the cheap stage first. (2) A POSITIVE DOES NOT BY ITSELF IDENTIFY BAG REACHABILITY -- it may be generic supervised document-side adaptation, which is what the mechanism control exists to separate. (3) BOTH DENSE COMPONENTS ARE CQADupStack FORUMS, so a gain licenses a CQADupStack-family claim, not broad out-of-domain reachability.
E14-HEAD.engineering_constraints: REGISTERED because they change what the code must be, not merely how it is written. (a) The head must be applied to evaluation documents as a LAZY slice-transforming view, driven by the scorer's own chunking: materializing headed float32 vectors is ~21.4 GB for HotpotQA and ~25.3 GB for the 6.17M-row pool, over this box's working limit. (b) Each patched scoring process emits exactly ONE head arm; any un-headed row produced inside such a process is rejected, since dev_eval.doc_vecs is shared across every variant in a process. (c) Every head artifact binds the table sha256, the Phase-B checkpoint sha256, the head-state sha256, the architecture, the head lr/seed/schedule, the train/holdout split hash and the M8 patch-source hashes -- a run_id alone does not stop a stale head being paired with a table.
E14-HEAD.shippability_gate: B6-pre PASSED with --head linear (results/m8_b6_pre.json) and with --head mlp (results/m8_b6_pre_mlp.json, 3,426 nodes, GELU as a plain Erf, zero custom-domain ops, parity 0.99999988). BOTH passes used identity/zero-ish weights, so before any head-bearing candidate is called shippable the ACTUAL TRAINED head must be exported and parity-tested -- a parity test that never leaves the identity path has not exercised the head.

D2.title: D2 -- compositional capacity: a multi-word tokenizer, trained through the forward
D2.registered: 2026-08-29, in the milestone audit and re-route (LEDGER 15). NO D2 number of any kind exists: no tokenizer has been trained, no arm has run, and the coverage precondition has not been measured. Every field here is legal in both directions.
D2.question: The table falls behind the teacher in proportion to how badly the query FRAGMENTS -- 0.050 nDCG per +1.0 subwords-per-word, t=4.61, surviving every single-dataset exclusion at t>=3.28 (LEDGER 17b). Does giving the table multi-word ROWS, so a query composes into fewer and longer units, recover any of that loss?
D2.why_this_probe_and_not_another: It is the only remaining lever in this milestone with a MEASURED mechanism pointing up. B3 closed data volume (~17.6x the pool to reach the bar), T1 closed the teacher (-0.052/-0.109), B2 closed the KL term, E14-HEAD closed the cheap doc-side head (-0.0244 dense), and M7's clean-stack tax closed licensing as the explanation (+0.0058, miss survives). Section 7 already records that the recipe/data class is hygiene rather than the route: M7's entire post-gate lever programme transferred to the six at 0.000 +/- 0.005. Both of D2's gates have PASSED -- B7 solves 128K rows in 17 s / 5.7 GB, B6-pre exports a fused doc graph with zero custom-domain ops.
D2.lever: A self-trained tokenizer over the training corpus with MULTI-WORD merges (merges permitted across the whitespace boundary), vocabulary V in {65536, 131072}, replacing bert-wordpiece-30522. Rows are trained through the forward under R0's recipe. This is the n-gram direction in non-overlapping form (LEDGER 13); additive n-gram rows on top of a unigram vocabulary are NOT part of this probe and are not revived by its outcome.
D2.held_fixed: Teacher (stella_en_400M_v5) and its document vectors; the pseudo-query pool and its draw seed; phase structure B->A; updates, batch, negatives (hard_neg_k=0), temperature, learning rates and schedules; precision int8; serving pool_mode sqrt; the frozen convex0 w=0.8 fusion operator; the query side stays a pure lookup table (E1) and the document side stays unheaded (D1 disabled). ONLY tokenizer_id, vocab and the row_init_construction they force may differ from R0.
D2.coverage_precondition: MEASURED BEFORE ANY TRAINING ARM, on a FIXED pool, and reported whatever it says. REBUILT 2026-08-29 after review: the previous version gated on the fraction of unique dev-reachable rows with zero updates, which is gameable by the vocabulary denominator (many one-occurrence rows dilute it) and was calibrated against M7's 5.71% OVERALL cold-row figure, a different quantity. Report instead: (a) dev token OCCURRENCE MASS assigned to rows with 0, <5 and <20 effective updates; (b) fraction of dev queries containing at least one such row; (c) the fraction of the section 17b fragmentation opportunity covered by adequately trained rows. GATE, performance-based rather than arbitrary: the sum-initialized, zero-residual compiled tokenizer must reproduce R0's dense out-of-domain macro to within 0.001 before any residual is trained. That is a direct test of the floor rather than a proxy for it, and it fails loudly if the compile is wrong.
D2.compositional_init_floor: MANDATORY, and it is the SUM of the constituent unigram rows, not the mean. CORRECTED 2026-08-29 after review: the served query is normalize(sum over types of g(count_t) * w_t), so replacing constituents a,b (each count 1) by a phrase row w_p = w_a + w_b leaves the summand IDENTICAL and the normalized query EXACTLY unchanged -- that is a true floor. The mean, (w_a+w_b)/2, changes the sum by -(w_a+w_b)/2, which is not a positive scalar multiple of the old sum, so normalization does NOT restore it and the phrase is silently downweighted ~2x against every other token. The earlier 'mean of constituent rows' specification was WRONG and would have degraded the baseline before any learning began. Phrase rows are then trained as a RESIDUAL on top of the sum init, so a row with too few updates stays at zero residual and reproduces R0 exactly rather than approximately. (For a constituent appearing more than once the sqrt saturation makes preservation approximate rather than exact; report the residual discrepancy, do not assume it away.)
D2.vocab_selection: TWO candidates, ONE finalist, selected on a NESTED DEV SPLIT THE BAR NEVER READS. Selection endpoint: the mean of the wikipedia group (nq-250k, hotpotqa) and the heldout group (heldout-train, heldout-longq), int8/sqrt, ONE seed per vocabulary. The bar reads the OUT-OF-DOMAIN macro (cqadup-programmers, cqadup-physics), which selection never touches, so the finalist is not chosen on the endpoint that judges it. Ties (|delta| < 0.0040 on the selection endpoint) break to the SMALLER vocabulary, on downloadable bytes -- the section 8 tie-break, fixed here before any number. TOKENIZER TRAINING IS DETERMINISTIC: the trainer is seeded and pinned, and the trained tokenizer's sha256 is recorded in the result, so tokenizer randomness contributes no variance the bar does not cover. Selection is over TWO pre-named vocabularies only; no third size may be added after seeing either.
D2.endpoint: PRIMARY and barred: DENSE = out-of-domain macro over cqadup-programmers and cqadup-physics, int8/sqrt -- the same scalar B3 and E14-HEAD read. SECONDARY and DESCRIPTIVE: the 4-component fused macro under the frozen operator, and the worst-group scalar. Reported always, adopted never.
D2.comparator: R0 at THREE INDEPENDENT FULL CHAINS, paired by chain seed. These ALREADY EXIST as section 23's crossed-grid diagonal -- (b0,a0), (b1,a1), (b2,a2) from work/runs/m8nf-seed0.json and m8nfb-seed{1,2}-{b,a}.json -- so the floor measurement already paid for D2's control and no R0 retraining is needed. Verify at run time that all three are readable as full chains in the incumbent frame before reading any D2 number; if any is not, retrain it rather than substituting an A-leg-only arm.
D2.bar: mean-over-seeds gain >= 0.00519 on the DENSE out-of-domain macro. 0.00519 is the registered section 4.7 formula 2 x 1.693 x sigma_chain with sigma_chain = 0.00153 measured by the crossed B x A design (section 23), ADOPTED for B-leg-varying arms by the 2026-08-29 audit amendment. D2 retrains the Phase-B checkpoint, so it is a chain-varying arm and 0.0040 -- the A-leg-only bar B3 and E14-HEAD read -- does NOT apply to it. Note sigma_chain is itself a floor on the floor (section 23: moment estimators clipped at zero, sqrt concave, ~8% low at this design), so 0.00519 is if anything permissive.
D2.bar_is_dense_only_and_why: The DENSE bar is the powered gate. FUSED IS NOT OPTIONAL ANY MORE (amended 2026-08-29): NF-CROSSED-FUSED must be measured and reported before any D2 success claim, and a dense-only win is labelled a MECHANISM success, never a release success. Why the fused endpoint is not a barred hypothesis: no chain-level fused floor existed when this was registered, and a 3-seed all-positive-sign fused condition would veto ~87.5% of genuine dense wins whose fused effect is real but too small to resolve (E14 measured fusion damping a dense change ~10x). THE COST IS STATED: B3 and E14-HEAD bought type-I protection from intersection-union across two scalars and D2 does not have it. For the dense claim alone there is no type-I inflation -- it is the same single hypothesis -- but the JOINT claim 'dense improves AND the fused system does not regress' is no longer tested, and that joint claim is the one release cares about. Fused is therefore reported with a pre-declared non-inferiority read against the measured chain-level fused floor, not a sign test.
D2.multiplicity: ONE contrast at the bar: the single finalist vocabulary against R0 on one endpoint. Vocabulary selection happens earlier, on a disjoint endpoint, and is NOT in the family -- that is what the nested split buys. No Holm correction is needed and none is applied. Registering it this way also removes the temptation to report whichever vocabulary won.
D2.step_adequacy: BOUNDED BY DESIGN, and the bound is the point. The E14-HEAD plateau heuristic is computed on a disjoint tuning seed and a training holdout. If it fires OPTIMIZATION-INADEQUATE, EXACTLY ONE continuation is permitted: the reported set at doubled steps WITH a paired doubled-step R0 (the budget cannot change for one arm alone -- the floor and the frozen recipe are both at 2,500). If that also misses, the class CLOSES. There is no third budget, no vocabulary escalation after a number, and no re-tokenized retry. E14-HEAD is the precedent this bound exists to avoid: an adequacy gate with no ceiling is a way never to take no for an answer, and D2 is the second lever in this milestone whose cheap predecessor failed and whose escalation was left 'open'.
D2.no_survivor: THE COMPOSITIONAL-CAPACITY ROUTE VIA NON-OVERLAPPING SEGMENTATION IS CLOSED -- and that is ALL it closes. AMENDED 2026-08-29 after review: the earlier text made a D2 miss plus a B10 miss sufficient to terminate the milestone, which was premature on this repository's own evidence. It does NOT close additive overlapping word/character n-gram rows (a DIFFERENT hypothesis class -- see ngram_rows_are_not_superseded), does not close hard-candidate listwise distillation (B2's teacher_top200 arm measures 0.777 nats mean entropy, and B2's own artifact names R-LIST as the consequence), and does not close E14-LORA (this ledger forbids the head result from closing it). The exit is correspondingly gated: see exit_precondition.
D2.prior_evidence_against: STATED UP FRONT so a negative is not read as a surprise. (1) The only published vocabulary-size ablation on a static/bag-of-words retriever is VDR (arXiv 2212.07699, ICLR 2024): 30K -> 110K rows moved BEIR nDCG@10 44.5 -> 42.6, a small REGRESSION. It is confounded (the vocabularies also swapped English for multilingual BERT and the authors blame the language mismatch), so it does not close D2, but it is the closest evidence and it points the wrong way. (2) M7 shipped with 1,743 rows (5.71%) never trained by either phase at a 30,522 vocabulary; 128K makes coverage the first question, not an afterthought. (3) See scope_limit for why section 17b's slope is not a forecast.
D2.scope_limit: SECTION 17b IS CORRELATED HEADROOM, NOT RECOVERABLE HEADROOM, and it is NOT A BOUND IN EITHER DIRECTION. Corrected 2026-08-29: the earlier text called it an upper bound, which is too generous. It is an uncontrolled between-query association fitted with ordinary query-level OLS (m8src/retention_decomp.py), so the slope may be driven entirely by specificity, rarity, domain, length or entity content -- D2 could recover none of it -- while conversely a phrase feature could exceed it through conjunction or denoising effects. No write-up may quote 0.050 x delta-fertility as a forecast in either direction. Arithmetic for scale only: clearing 0.00519 on the gap slope needs a fertility reduction of ~0.104 against a pooled fertility of ~1.375 (~7.5%), mechanically reachable at 64-128K; but on the TABLE's own slope (-0.0121) it would need ~0.41. Both dense components are CQADupStack forums, so a D2 result is a CQADupStack-family dev result.
D2.engineering_constraints: E7 cap binds the TOTAL downloadable query-side system (int8 table + tokenizer artifacts + ONNX container) at 233 MB: 65,536 x 1024 int8 = 65.8 MB, 131,072 x 1024 int8 = 131.6 MB, both fit with room for a large tokenizer, and the tokenizer's own bytes count and must be reported. B7 measured the solver at both sizes (65,536: 51 its / 10 s / 4.4 GB; 131,072: 68 its / 17 s / 5.7 GB) so neither vocabulary is gated on the solver. B6-pre's PASS used near-identity weights, so the ACTUAL trained table must be re-exported before anything is called shippable. G5 applies: smoke every new path, write the wall-clock estimate before launch and check the rate in the slow region, setsid nohup for anything over 10 minutes.
D2.cost_estimate: TO BE MEASURED BEFORE LAUNCH, NOT TRUSTED FROM THIS FIELD (CLAUDE.md: never trust a docstring's cost estimate -- two in m7src/train.py were wrong by two orders of magnitude on the same day). Shape: tokenizer training x2 (minutes), the coverage measurement (no training), 2 selection chains at 1 seed, 3 finalist chains at 3 seeds = 5 new full B->A chains, plus scoring. R0's three chains already exist. Compositional init needs no new teacher forwards.
D2.bar_frozen: 2026-08-29, in the audit amendment, before any tokenizer was trained.
D2.authorised_by: LEDGER 8 (D2 is on the Stage-S menu), LEDGER 9 (Wave-1 promotion of its gates), and the 2026-08-29 milestone audit amendment in LEDGER 15.
D2.plan_status: LIVE -- first in line, but GATED BY D2-PRE. Not 'the only remaining route'.
D2.amended: 2026-08-29, after a Codex adversarial review of this registration, BEFORE any arm ran and before any tokenizer was trained. Three BLOCKERs and several MAJORs adopted; see LEDGER 15. The changes: mean-constituent init REPLACED by sum (the mean is not a floor); the pool-expansion escape clause REMOVED; the coverage gate rebuilt on occurrence mass plus a baseline-preservation check; NF-CROSSED-FUSED made MANDATORY before any success claim; tokenizer training pinned deterministic; and D2 demoted from 'the only remaining route' to 'first in line', because non-overlapping segmentation does NOT subsume additive overlapping n-gram rows.
D2.pool_is_fixed: NO POOL EXPANSION INSIDE D2. The earlier coverage clause permitted 'expand the pool and re-measure', which contradicted held_fixed and was a BLOCKER: an expanded pool invalidates the pre-existing R0 chains as controls and makes the arm POOL-varying, which section 23's crossed floor explicitly does not bound, so 0.00519 would not be calibrated for it. If a vocabulary cannot be covered by the fixed pool, the answer is the smaller vocabulary or a NO-GO -- never a bigger pool. Pool expansion is a separate intervention needing its own registration, its own pool-varying floor and fresh paired controls.
D2.exit_precondition: THE PRE-COMMITTED EXIT MAY NOT FIRE UNTIL D2, B10, B8 AND R-LIST HAVE ALL RUN AND MISSED, and until the standing directive in CLAUDE.md has been re-run at that point (best-component arithmetic, every failure diagnosed, literature swept, capability claims checked algebraically, and the reopening condition named). A pre-commitment cannot perform a future milestone audit in advance; it can only bind the DEFAULT, which remains: do not spend the reserved access without a credible release candidate. B8 is included because it is a closed-form document-centroid target costing ~15 minutes plus scoring -- deferring it is a false economy. R-LIST is included because B2 directly triggered it.
D2.ngram_rows_are_not_superseded: REGISTERED CORRECTION 2026-08-29 (Codex MAJOR, algebraically confirmed). LEDGER section 13's 'n-gram rows are superseded by D2' collapses two different hypothesis classes and is WITHDRAWN as a blanket rule. D2 picks ONE segmentation and REMOVES the constituent activations; additive overlapping rows KEEP the incumbent unigrams and may fire several overlapping phrases at once. Decisively: an additive phrase row with ZERO residual recovers R0 EXACTLY, whereas a segmentation change does not do so automatically -- so the additive class is strictly the safer parameterisation of the same intuition. Character n-grams additionally reach rare and unseen technical strings a frequency tokenizer may never allocate a token to. D2-PRE compares the classes at equal row budget before either is committed to full chains.

NF-CROSSED-FUSED.title: NF-CROSSED-FUSED -- the chain-level FUSED floor, from cells already on disk
NF-CROSSED-FUSED.registered: 2026-08-29, milestone audit. Cheap and optional: it does not gate D2, it upgrades D2's bar if it lands first.
NF-CROSSED-FUSED.question: Section 23's crossed B x A grid was scored DENSE only, so no chain-level fused floor exists and no B-leg-varying arm can carry a barred fused endpoint. What is sigma_chain on the fused macro?
NF-CROSSED-FUSED.lever: NONE -- no training. Nine existing crossed cells (work/runs/m8nfx-* plus the diagonal) scored through the frozen convex0 w=0.8 operator, APPLIED and never re-fitted (section 4.7b: re-fitting per arm measures the floor of a fitting procedure, a different and much larger quantity).
NF-CROSSED-FUSED.held_fixed: Everything. The cells exist; this is a scoring pass.
NF-CROSSED-FUSED.endpoint: fused macro over the frozen spec's four components, int8/sqrt.
NF-CROSSED-FUSED.comparator: none -- this measures the instrument, exactly as NF does.
NF-CROSSED-FUSED.bar: NO BAR: this is a floor measurement, exempt from noise calibration under section 4.7's named exemption for arithmetic and instrument reads. Its OUTPUT is a bar: 2 x 1.693 x sigma_chain(fused), adopted for B-leg-varying arms by amendment, or the planning minimum 0.0040 if that is larger.
NF-CROSSED-FUSED.multiplicity: none -- one variance decomposition on one endpoint.
NF-CROSSED-FUSED.no_survivor: NOT APPLICABLE -- a floor cannot fail. AMENDED 2026-08-29: the earlier text let this probe's consequence turn on whether D2 could 'plausibly clear' the resulting bar, an undefined judgement and therefore exploitable. Removed. The measurement is MANDATORY before any D2 success claim, its number is reported whatever it is, and the fused read is a pre-declared non-inferiority comparison against it.
NF-CROSSED-FUSED.authorised_by: LEDGER 15, 2026-08-29 audit amendment; section 4.7's exemption for instrument reads.
NF-CROSSED-FUSED.plan_status: LIVE and MANDATORY before a D2 success claim (was 'optional').

D2-PRE.title: D2-PRE -- closed-form preflight: does ANY new-row class carry residual capacity, and which?
D2-PRE.registered: 2026-08-29, adopted from the Codex review of D2's registration, before any tokenizer was trained.
D2-PRE.question: D2 costs five full B->A chains. Before spending them: do new rows contain useful residual capacity at all, and does NON-OVERLAPPING segmentation beat ADDITIVE OVERLAPPING rows at an equal row budget? Section 17b's fertility slope cannot answer either -- it is correlated headroom, so it motivates a diagnostic, not a training programme.
D2-PRE.lever: NO TRAINING CHAINS. One deterministic 64K tokenizer, then closed-form ridge residual solves on frozen incumbent rows using m8src/blockcg.py (B7: 17 s at 131,072 rows). Four arms at EQUAL added-row budget: (a) D2 non-overlapping segmentation; (b) additive overlapping WORD n-gram rows; (c) additive CHARACTER n-gram rows; (d) D2 plus zero-residual cold-row fallback.
D2-PRE.held_fixed: Teacher, document vectors, the pool, and every incumbent row. Only the added rows are solved for.
D2-PRE.staged_checks: IN ORDER, each able to stop the probe. (1) OPPORTUNITY: retokenize dev+train queries and measure the actual fertility reduction, especially on the high-gap queries section 17b identifies -- if the out-of-domain reduction is far below ~0.104 then even the optimistic association cannot reach 0.00519 and D2 is not worth five chains. (2) COMPILE/FLOOR: sum-initialize the new rows, zero residual, score against R0 -- must reproduce R0 within 0.001 dense. Mean init is scored beside it as a NEGATIVE CONTROL and is expected to be worse; if it is not, the pooling model in this registration is wrong and everything downstream stops. (3) RESIDUAL: solve only the new rows against the existing teacher-query targets, cross-fitted so the scored dataset's own queries never enter the fit (B17's lesson: a probe that fits and scores on the same small set measures its fit set).
D2-PRE.endpoint: dense out-of-domain macro at int8/sqrt, closed-form tables only -- the same scalar D2's bar reads, so the preflight and the probe are commensurable.
D2-PRE.comparator: R0's shipped table in the identical frame, plus the sum-init zero-residual compile as the exact floor.
D2-PRE.bar: DIAGNOSTIC AND ROUTING, not an adoption -- no candidate may ship from a closed-form fit, and no bar is cleared here. Registered routing, fixed before the number: authorise full D2 chains ONLY IF the closed-form best arm shows (i) a clearly positive sign on the dense endpoint, (ii) headroom plausibly above 0.00519 rather than marginally at it, (iii) coverage adequate by occurrence mass, and (iv) no material fused degradation. If an ADDITIVE arm beats the segmentation arm at equal row budget, the additive class is registered as the capacity lever INSTEAD of D2 and D2 stands down -- that reversal is registered now, before the number, precisely so it cannot be argued away later.
D2-PRE.multiplicity: Descriptive comparison across four arms; no hypothesis test and no family. Its output is a routing decision, and the routing rule above is fixed in advance.
D2-PRE.no_survivor: NO new-row class carries closed-form residual capacity. That is a strong and cheap argument against spending five chains on ANY of them, and it is the outcome that would make the compositional-capacity direction closable on evidence rather than on budget. It does not by itself fire the milestone exit -- see D2's exit_precondition.
D2-PRE.why_closed_form_is_informative_here: Because M7 and M8 both already use closed-form distilled tables as a screening instrument that TRACKS the trained artifact: T1 ranked teachers on exactly this criterion, and B7's real-data run reproduced M7's trained dev macro (0.3439) at the argmax lambda. Its known failure mode is documented and guarded against: B17 fired a registered branch on a 957-query fit set and was DISOWNED because the same class scored 0.3439 on 350K queries. Hence the cross-fitting requirement and hence 'routing, never adoption'.
D2-PRE.cost_estimate: Target under one hour, MEASURED not assumed (G5). Tokenizer training minutes; block-CG solves seconds each; scoring dominates.
D2-PRE.plan_status: LIVE -- run this BEFORE D2's chains.

dev_aggregation.selection: median of the three group means
dev_aggregation.worst_group: min of the three group means
dev_aggregation.band_provenance: the smallest effect this project has ever adopted (M7 lever #4)

legs.C2: M8 int8 query TABLE > M7 int8 query TABLE on the SAME frozen incumbent document vectors, D1 DISABLED. If the teacher swaps this is unsatisfiable and C2 reverts to the registered alternative: the dense SYSTEM comparison, each on its own teacher's document vectors, D1 still disabled (LEDGER 4.2).

legs_per_hypothesis: Holm-corrected signflip rejection at family alpha
raw one-sided lower bound at alpha/3 > 0, same draws
ship_rule.six_set_margin_provenance: 2.4x the measured near-sibling six-macro paired SE (0.0026-0.0032, from results/perquery.json: leaf-ir-asym vs mdbr-leaf-ir 0.00263, LR-dense-pertask vs LR-dense-websearch 0.00316). P(false veto | truly equal) ~ 0.99; ~80% power against a true regression of ~0.0135.
ship_rule.unknown_key_policy: FAIL -- a key on neither list fails the qualifying condition; classification happens at manifest time, before the access
ship_rule.c2_form_selector: same_teacher -> table-vs-table on identical doc vectors; teacher_swapped -> dense-system-vs-dense-system. Selected by a fact fixed at pipeline step 5, before any M8 number.
ship_rule.six_set_read_timing: scored after the freeze, inside the guarded access process, BEFORE the reserved payloads are opened, written atomically, logged to m8/SIX_ACCESS.log. It is NOT a decision point: the reserved access proceeds regardless of what it says, and nothing about the candidate may change after it. It governs shipping, not measuring.
ship_rule._key_schema_note: EVERY key a candidate manifest can carry is classified here, NOW, while the amendment is legal. The space is train.Cfg's 35 fields plus the artifact-level fields a release records. An unclassified key FAILS condition 4 by design -- but leaving foreseeable keys unclassified would turn the condition into a coin decided by naming conventions at manifest time, which is the opposite of a pre-registration (2026-08-29 review finding).

neutral_keys._why: keys that describe the FRAME rather than a lever. They are neither qualifying nor disqualifying, and they are enumerated so they do not fall through to 'unknown'.

ship_rule.teacher_swap_note: A teacher swap flips teacher_id/encoder_spec (NEUTRAL) and, if it changes tokenizer, also tokenizer_id and vocab -- which ARE qualifying-table keys. That is a side effect of the swap, not an E11-sense v2 lever, so a swap alone must NOT satisfy condition 4: the manifest must declare at least one qualifying_table key that is not tokenizer_id or vocab whenever a teacher swap is in the diff. Registered now, before any swap exists.

shadow_gate.set: LoTTE, forum queries only, surviving slices from S0
shadow_gate.endpoint: equal-weight macro of nDCG@10 over surviving slices, exact search
shadow_gate.comparator: the frozen M7 released system on the identical slices
shadow_gate.go_rule: GO iff BOTH (a) LoTTE surviving-slice macro delta >= -0.0068 (non-regression at the MDE scale) AND (b) dev worst-group >= +0.0068

branches.NO-GO: defer to M9, panel preserved (default) or report-only

noise_floor.floor_statistic: max over the 3 pairwise |delta| on that endpoint
noise_floor.bar_formula: bar(endpoint) = max(planning_minimum, 2 x floor(endpoint)); planning_minimum never below 0.0040
noise_floor.also_published: the +/-10% A-steps perturbation, reported as recipe sensitivity BESIDE the floor, never AS the floor

measured.dense: results/m8_noise_floor.json -- floors 0.00095-0.00227, bars 0.0040 except fp16.mean worst-group/OOD at 0.00454
measured.still_missing: a POOL-varying null. The B-leg gap is now measured (see 'crossed'), but all nine cells share one pseudo-query pool -- pseudoq.build_decontaminated draws with a seed independent of the training seed -- so no floor here bounds a lever that changes the pool itself.
measured.crossed: results/m8_noise_floor_crossed.json -- the 3x3 (B checkpoint seed) x (A seed) grid, LEDGER 23. MEASURED: on the out-of-domain macro sigma_B 0.00103 vs sigma_A 0.00106, sigma_chain 0.00153, so a B-leg-varying arm's null is about sqrt(2) times an A-leg arm's and the standing 0.0040 carries ~6.5% type-I there. Bars in force are UNAFFECTED: B3 and E14-HEAD read A-leg-only arms, whose null is sigma_A alone (2 x 1.693 x 0.00106 = 0.0036, under the planning minimum). For a B-leg-varying probe the formula with the floor term estimated from this design would give 0.00519 -- REPORTED, NOT ADOPTED, since changing the floor estimator is itself a formula change needing its own amendment.
